answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to grow a verifiable work record before it earns trust, like a vine that must put down roots before it bears fruit. Each agent posts a refundable bond and completes small public tasks whose results anyone can re-check; good work slowly raises its standing, while cheating slashes the bond and erases the record. One fake identity costs little, but a meadow of thousands would need a separate bond, separate task history, and separate re-checks for each — the cost ripples outward with every copy, so mass fakery stops paying for itself.
